PHYS 100.title: Introductory Physics
PHYS 100.description: Kinematics, force, energy, momentum, use of graphs and vectors in physics; thermal energy, heat transfer, Earth's energy balance; electricity. Students with credit for Physics 12 may not obtain credit for this course unless they took AP, IB, or A-level Physics and were offered advanced credit for PHYS 100.

children.raw: Not open to students with credit for

PHYS 100.prerequisiteText: Not open to students with credit for PHYS 12
notes: Principles of Mathematics 12 or Pre-calculus 12 is required; Physics 11 is required for first-year students, strongly recommended for others.

PHYS 101.title: Energy and Waves
PHYS 101.description: Fluids, harmonic oscillator, travelling waves, standing waves, sound, and interference of light waves, including diffraction.
PHYS 101.corequisiteText: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184

PHYS 102.title: Electricity, Light and Radiation
PHYS 102.description: Introduction to optics, electricity and magnetism, electric circuits, radioactivity, including biological applications.
PHYS 102.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121

PHYS 106.title: Enriched Physics 1 (lecture)
PHYS 106.description: Classical mechanics including conservation laws, angular momentum of rigid bodies and simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, with an introduction to special relativity, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical mechanics and solid state physics.
PHYS 106.prerequisiteText: Either (a) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, MATH 12 or (b) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, PREC 12 or (c) a score more than 85% in all of PHYS 12, CALC 12 or (d) a score more than 85% in PHYS 100. PHYS 12 = Physics 12; MATH 12 = Principles of Mathematics 12; PREC 12 = Pre-Calculus 12; CALC 12 = Calculus 12
PHYS 106.corequisiteText: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184

PHYS 107.title: Enriched Physics 1
PHYS 107.description: Classical mechanics including conservation laws, angular momentum of rigid bodies and simple harmonic motion, wave phenomena, with an introduction to special relativity, quantum mechanics, nuclear physics, statistical mechanics and solid state physics.

PHYS 107.prerequisiteText: Either (a) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, MATH 12 or (b) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, PREC 12 or (c) a score of 85% or higher in all of PHYS 12, CALC 12 or (d) a score of 85% or higher in PHYS 100. MATH 12 = Principles of Mathematics 12; PREC 12 = Pre-Calculus 12; CALC 12 = Calculus 12; PHYS 12 = Physics 12
PHYS 107.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184

PHYS 108.title: Enriched Physics II
PHYS 108.description: Electricity and magnetism, electrical circuits, induction, electromagnetic waves, Maxwell's equations and applications.

children.raw: a score of 85% or higher in

PHYS 108.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107 or (b) a score of 85% or higher in one of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131
PHYS 108.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121

PHYS 109.title: Enriched Experimental Physics
PHYS 109.description: A laboratory course accompanying PHYS 108 with emphasis on data collection and analysis and experimental techniques.

PHYS 117.title: Dynamics and Waves
PHYS 117.description: Kinematics including curvilinear motion. Forces and Newton's laws of motion. Work-energy theorem, conservation of energy. Conservation of momentum, collisions. Torque, rotational dynamics, angular momentum. Oscillations and waves.
PHYS 117.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100

PHYS 118.title: Electricity, Light and Radiation
PHYS 118.description: Optics, electricity and magnetism, electric circuits, electromagnetic waves.
PHYS 118.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS_V 101, PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 131, PHYS_V 157 and one of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184
PHYS 118.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121

PHYS 119.title: Experimental Physics Lab I
PHYS 119.description: Introductory laboratory course, with emphasis on data collection, data analysis techniques, and scientific reasoning.
PHYS 119.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100

PHYS 129.title: Experimental Physics Lab II
PHYS 129.description: A second laboratory course emphasizing the synthesis and development of further sophistication around the data collection, data analysis techniques and scientific reasoning developed in PHYS 119.

PHYS 131.title: Energy and Waves (Lecture)
PHYS 131.description: Fluids, harmonic oscillator, travelling waves, standing waves, sound, and interference of light waves, radioactivity including biological applications.
PHYS 131.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 100, MATH_V 102, MATH_V 104, MATH_V 110, MATH_V 120, MATH_V 180, MATH_V 184, MATH_O 100

PHYS 153.title: Elements of Physics
PHYS 153.description: Thermometry, thermal properties of matter, heat, oscillations, waves, sound, wave optics; geometrical optics, elementary electricity and magnetism, simple DC and AC circuits.
PHYS 153.corequisiteText: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184

PHYS 157.title: Introductory Physics for Engineers I
PHYS 157.description: Heat, thermodynamics, oscillations, waves, and sound.
PHYS 157.corequisiteText: One of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184

PHYS 158.title: Introductory Physics for Engineers II
PHYS 158.description: Electricity and magnetism, DC and AC circuits, optics.
PHYS 158.corequisiteText: One of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121

PHYS 159.title: Introductory Physics Laboratory for Engineers
PHYS 159.description: A laboratory course with emphasis on experimental design, measurement and analysis techniques.

PHYS 170.title: Mechanics I
PHYS 170.description: Statics of particles, equilibrium or rigid bodies, rigid body statics and internal forces, trusses; kinematics: rectilinear motion; dynamics: Newton's second law, friction, impulse, momentum, work and energy. Recommended pre-requisites: one of PHYS 12, PHYS 100 and one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 120, MATH 180, MATH 184. Recommended co-requisite: one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121.

PHYS 200.title: Relativity and Quanta
PHYS 200.description: Special relativity: Lorentz transformation, dynamics and conservation laws. Quantum physics: the experimental evidence for quantization; a qualitative discussion of the concepts of quantum mechanics and their application to simple systems of atoms and nuclei.
PHYS 200.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 153 and one of MATH_V 101, MATH_V 103, MATH_V 105, MATH_V 121, MATH_O 101, MATH_O 103; or (b) SCIE 001

PHYS 203.title: Thermal Physics I
PHYS 203.description: Fundamentals of thermodynamics and statistical physics; entropy, laws of thermodynamics, heat engines, free energy, phase transitions, Boltzmann statistics, quantum statistics.
PHYS 203.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 153, PHYS_V 158, SCIE_V 001
PHYS 203.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200

PHYS 209.title: Intermediate Experimental Physics
PHYS 209.description: Use of analog electronics and amplifiers, digital electronics and analog-to-digital conversion and the use of computers in data analysis and simulations in thermodynamic, electronic and modern physics experiments.
PHYS 209.prerequisiteText: Either (a) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 109 or (b) one of PHYS 102, PHYS 153 or (c) SCIE 001 or (d) all of PHYS 158, PHYS 159 or (e) all of PHYS 118, PHYS 119 or (f) all of PHYS 108, PHYS 119
PHYS 209.corequisiteText: One of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258 and one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254

PHYS 210.title: Introduction to Computational Physics
PHYS 210.description: Introduction to UNIX/Linux; software tools for processing, fitting and displaying data; numerical methods and application in the physical sciences.
PHYS 210.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS_V 102, PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118, PHYS_V 153, PHYS_V 158, SCIE_V 001
PHYS 210.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222

PHYS 216.title: Intermediate Mechanics
PHYS 216.description: Review of kinematics, Newton's laws, angular momentum and fixed axis rotation. Rigid body motion, central forces, non-inertial frames of reference. Introduction to Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics.
PHYS 216.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS_V 106, PHYS_V 107, PHYS_V 117, PHYS_V 170, SCIE_V 001, PHYS_O 111 and one of MATH_V 152, MATH_V 221, MATH_V 223, MATH_O 222
PHYS 216.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_V 254, MATH_O 200

PHYS 219.title: Intermediate Experimental Physics I
PHYS 219.description: Analog electronics and amplifiers, digital electronics, analog-to-digital converters and an introduction to use of computers in data analysis and simulations.
PHYS 219.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of PHYS_V 108, PHYS_V 118 and one of PHYS_V 109, PHYS_V 119 or (b) PHYS_V 102 or (c) all of PHYS_V 158, PHYS_V 159 or (d) SCIE_V 001
PHYS 219.corequisiteText: One of MATH_V 200, MATH_V 217, MATH_V 226, MATH_V 253, MATH_O 200

PHYS 229.title: Intermediate Experimental Physics II
PHYS 229.description: Thermodynamics experiments, modern physics experiments and use of computers in data analysis.

PHYS 250.title: Introduction to Modern Physics
PHYS 250.description: Wave-particle duality of matter, special relativity, processes in atomic, nuclear and solid state, and introduction to quantum mechanical devices and techniques.
PHYS 250.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 158, PHYS 153, SCIE 001

PHYS 298.title: Co-operative Work Placement I
PHYS 298.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the winter term of the second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics.

PHYS 299.title: Co-operative Work Placement II
PHYS 299.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the second year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics.

PHYS 301.title: Electricity and Magnetism
PHYS 301.description: Maxwell's equations and their applications, electrical fields and potentials of static charge distributions, current, fields of moving charges, magnetic fields, electromagnetic induction.
PHYS 301.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 153, PHYS 158, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 317 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255

PHYS 304.title: Introduction to Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 304.description: Principles and applications of quantum mechanics, wave mechanics, the Schroedinger equation, expectation values, Hermitian operators, commuting observables, one-dimensional systems, harmonic oscillators, angular momentum, three-dimensional systems.

PHYS 305.title: Introduction to Biophysics
PHYS 305.description: Physical principles involved in biological systems at the microscopic and molecular scales. Diffusion, low Reynolds number dynamics, the physicist's view of biomolecular structure, models of molecular motors and membranes.
PHYS 305.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 153, PHYS 158, SCIE 001 and either (a) PHYS 203 or (b) one of ENPH 257, CHEM 201, CHEM 205 and one of MATH 302, MATH 318, STAT 241, STAT 251, STAT 302

PHYS 306.title: Advanced Mechanics
PHYS 306.description: Variational calculus, Lagrangian dynamics, rigid body motion including free and forced precession, Hamiltonian mechanics, Poisson brackets, canonical coordinates, Hamilton-Jacobi theory, action angle variables. Introduction to dynamical chaos: determinism, Lyapunov exponents.
PHYS 306.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 216, ENPH 270 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255, MATH 256, MATH 258

PHYS 309.title: Electrical Laboratory
PHYS 309.description: Selected experiments in electromagnetism and electronics; computer data acquisition; advanced data analysis and simulation.

PHYS 310.title: Machine Learning for Physics and Astronomy Data Analysis
PHYS 310.description: Fundamental principles and applications of data-centric research techniques in Physics and Astronomy. Topics include algorithms for data structuring, dimensionality reduction, linear regression and classification, artificial neural nets, convolutional neural nets, unsupervised learning.
PHYS 310.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 152, MATH 221, MATH 223 and one of MATH 200, MATH 217, MATH 226, MATH 253, MATH 254 and one of BIOL 300, STAT 200, STAT 203, STAT 241, STAT 251, MATH 318 and one of PHYS 210, CPSC 103, CPSC 110, APSC 160, EOSC 211 and one of PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 158, SCIE 001

PHYS 312.title: Introduction to Mathematical Physics
PHYS 312.description: The application of ordinary and partial differential equations to physical problems; boundary and initial value problems associated with heat, wave and Laplace equations. Fourier analysis; expansions in Bessel and Legendre functions.

PHYS 314.title: Fluids
PHYS 314.description: Kinetic theory: Diffusion, viscosity and sound waves. Introduction to hydrodynamics: Laminar flow, capillary and gravity waves, convection and turbulence. Dimensional analysis.

PHYS 315.title: Quantum Physics of Materials
PHYS 315.description: Crystal structure, elasticity and phonons, elementary electronic transport, defects, alloys, liquid crystals and polymers.
PHYS 315.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 203, ENPH 257, CHEM 201, CHEM 205, CHEM 304 and one of PHYS 200, PHYS 250, CHEM 312

PHYS 318.title: Experimental Acoustics
PHYS 318.description: Experimental techniques of acoustics: data acquisition hardware and software, microphones, loudspeakers, noise, vibration and modal analysis.

PHYS 319.title: Electronics Laboratory
PHYS 319.description: A project-oriented lab introducing the design and construction of microprocessor-controlled devices.

PHYS 330.title: Modern Physics
PHYS 330.description: Quantum physics, nuclear energy and particle physics at a level suitable for third- and fourth-year Science students not proceeding to a physics degree. Not for credit towards a B.Sc. in Astronomy, Biophysics or Physics.
PHYS 330.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH 100, MATH 102, MATH 104, MATH 110, MATH 180, MATH 184 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157; or (b) SCIE 001

PHYS 333.title: Energy and Climate
PHYS 333.description: The fundamental physics behind global issues of energy use and climate change.
PHYS 333.prerequisiteText: Either (a) one of MATH 101, MATH 103, MATH 105, MATH 121 and one of PHYS 101, PHYS 102, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 108, PHYS 117, PHYS 118, PHYS 131, PHYS 153, PHYS 157, PHYS 158; or (b) SCIE 001

PHYS 340.title: Revolutions in Understanding the Universe
PHYS 340.description: Ancient Greek ideas of substance and forms and modern concepts of forces and fields. The twentieth-century quantum revolution. The modern universe, from quarks and atoms to the big bang. Quantum paradoxes. Not for credit in the faculties of Science and Applied Science. No mathematics beyond Grade 10 required.

PHYS 341.title: Physics of Music
PHYS 341.description: An introduction to the physical principles important to the production, transmission and perception of musical sounds. The treatment will be non-mathematical; with emphasis on demonstrations. Topics may include the description of sound waves, resonances, scales, physics of hearing, examination of specific musical instruments, etc. Not for credit in the Faculties of Science and Applied Science.

PHYS 343.title: Physical Science by Inquiry
PHYS 343.description: A guided sequence of hands-on science modules intended primarily for prospective elementary schoolteachers, to help them to work constructively in a science teaching role. Not for credit in the Faculties of Science and Applied Science.

PHYS 348.title: Frontiers in Physics and Astronomy
PHYS 348.description: Current research topics in physics and astronomy are investigated and explored. Technical communication and research skills are studied and developed via oral presentations and written scientific reports on these current research topics.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing in a physics honours program or fourth-year standing in a physics or astronomy major program

PHYS 348.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing in a physics honours program or fourth-year standing in a physics or astronomy major program

PHYS 349.title: Directed Research Project in Physics
PHYS 349.description: A research project, undertaken under the direction of a faculty member, culminating in a written report. This course requires approval of the course instructor and program advisor in the Department of Physics and Astronomy.

PHYS 350.title: Applications of Classical Mechanics
PHYS 350.description: Review of principles. Particle mechanics: Euler's equations, tops and gyroscopes, motion of the Earth, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian methods. Variational principles in optics and mechanics, Liouville's theorem and statistical mechanics. The relationship between classical and quantum mechanics.

PHYS 354.title: Electric and Magnetic Fields
PHYS 354.description: Applications of electricity and magnetism. Maxwell's equations.
PHYS 354.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 153, SCIE 001 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255 and one of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 317

PHYS 399.title: Co-operative Work Placement III
PHYS 399.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the third year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics.

PHYS 400.title: Introduction to Elementary Particles
PHYS 400.description: Standard model, classification of elementary particles and forces of nature, symmetries, conservation laws, quark model, quantum electrodynamics, quantum chromodynamics, and the theory of weak interactions.

PHYS 401.title: Electromagnetic Theory
PHYS 401.description: Applications of Maxwell's theory. Wave propagation in dielectrics, conductors and plasmas, wave guides, radiation, antennae, and special relativity.

PHYS 402.title: Applications of Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 402.description: Spin and angular momentum addition, perturbation methods, and applications in the fields of Atomic, Molecular, Nuclear, and Solid State Physics.

PHYS 403.title: Statistical Mechanics
PHYS 403.description: Principles and applications of statistical mechanics. Ideal gases, degenerate Fermi gases, Bose-Einstein condensation, black body radiation, fluctuations and phase transitions.
PHYS 403.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 203, ENPH 257, PHYS 257, CHEM 201, CHEM 304 and one of PHYS 304, PHYS 450, CHEM 312
notes: One of MATH 302, MATH 318, STAT 241, STAT 251, STAT 302 is recommended.

PHYS 404.title: Introduction to Medical Physics
PHYS 404.description: Radiotherapy, X-ray imaging, nuclear medicine, magnetic resonance imaging and biomedical optics.

prerequisite.raw: Third year standing in Science or Applied Science is required

PHYS 404.prerequisiteText: Third year standing in Science or Applied Science is required
notes: MATH 200 (or MATH 217 or MATH 226) is recommended.

PHYS 405.title: Radiation Biophysics
PHYS 405.description: Physical and chemical interactions of ionizing radiations and their biological effects at the cellular, tissue and whole-animal levels.

children.raw: third year standing in Science or Applied Science

PHYS 405.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 102, PHYS 108, PHYS 118, PHYS 153, PHYS 158, SCIE 001. and third year standing in Science or Applied Science

PHYS 407.title: Introduction to General Relativity
PHYS 407.description: Physical consequences of Einstein's equations, including the principle of equivalence, curved space-time, geodesics, the Schwarzschild solution, deflection of light, black holes, and gravitational radiation.
PHYS 407.prerequisiteText: One of MATH 217, MATH 227, MATH 317 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255
notes: PHYS 301 and one of PHYS 206, PHYS 306 are recommended.

PHYS 408.title: Optics
PHYS 408.description: Principles and applications of optical physics. Interference, diffraction, coherence, polarization, Fresnel relations, optical coatings, waves in dielectric media, Gaussian beams, waveguides, optical cavities, lasers, fibre optics, and Fourier optics.
PHYS 408.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 301, PHYS 354 and one of MATH 215, MATH 255

PHYS 409.title: Experimental Physics
PHYS 409.description: A laboratory course with a wide choice of experiments for fourth year Honours and Major students. Topics include solid state, nuclear, classical, quantum, electromagnetic and low temperature physics. For six credits, two weekly laboratory periods and completion of a project in second term are required.

PHYS 410.title: Computational Physics
PHYS 410.description: Scientific programming applied to problems in physics. Fundamentals of numerical analysis for continuum problems. Solution of linear and non-linear algebraic systems, ordinary differential equations and stochastic problems.
PHYS 410.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 312, MATH 257, MATH 316 and one of PHYS 210, EOSC 211, CPSC 110, CPSC 103, APSC 160

PHYS 412.title: Quantum Physics
PHYS 412.description: Fundamentals of atomic, nuclear, particle, and condensed matter physics.
PHYS 412.prerequisiteText: MATH 215 and one of CHEM 312, PHYS 200

PHYS 420.title: Physics Demonstrations
PHYS 420.description: The students will prepare, under the supervision of a faculty member, a demonstration or series of demonstrations intended to illustrate physical principles to diverse audiences. Intended for third- or fourth-year Physics Majors and Math/Science Education students.

PHYS 437.title: Physics of Biocellular Structure and Machinery
PHYS 437.description: Molecular structure and architecture of biological cells, interactions of molecules in aqueous solution and at interfaces, physical properties of polymers and surfactants, mechanisms of cell membranes and cytoplasmic structures, thermodynamics of molecular machines and mechanical enzymes. Credit can not be given for both PHYS_V 437 and 537.
PHYS 437.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS_V 313, PHYS_V 403, PHYS_V 455, CHEM_V 304

PHYS 438.title: Zoological Physics
PHYS 438.description: Animal systems viewed from a physicist's perspective. Topics include sensory systems, energy budgets, locomotion, internal flows, physical advantages of grouping.
PHYS 438.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 101, PHYS 106, PHYS 107, PHYS 117, PHYS 131, PHYS 157, SCIE 001

PHYS 447.title: Advanced Topics in Physics
PHYS 447.description: Directed studies available to students in Honours Physics with approval from the Head of the Department.

PHYS 449.title: Honours Thesis
PHYS 449.description: A research project, undertaken under the direction of a faculty member, culminating in a thesis.

PHYS 450.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 450.description: Postulates of quantum mechanics, expectation values, hermitian operators, commuting observables, applications to one-dimensional systems, harmonic oscillators, angular momentum, applications in three dimensions, hydrogen atom, time dependent perturbations.

PHYS 454.title: Applied Electromagnetic Theory
PHYS 454.description: Wave propagation and related phenomena in dielectrics, conductors and plasmas. Wave guides, radiation, antennae, special relativity.

PHYS 455.title: Statistical Mechanics
PHYS 455.description: Introduction to quantum statistical mechanics and its application to systems of varying complexity from the simple ideal gas to the degenerate gas. Quantum fluids, phase transitions and simulation methods will also be introduced.
PHYS 455.prerequisiteText: One of PHYS 257, PHYS 203, PHYS 313 and one of PHYS 304, PHYS 450

PHYS 458.title: Applied Optics
PHYS 458.description: Basic applications of lasers, geometrical optics, fibre optics, diffraction, and Fourier optics.

PHYS 473.title: Applied Nuclear Physics
PHYS 473.description: Radioactive decay and radiations, nuclear properties, interactions of neutrons, physical principles of power reactors, nuclear fusion, radiation monitoring, and safety.

PHYS 474.title: Applied Solid State Physics
PHYS 474.description: Symmetry of crystal structures, reciprocal lattice, band theory, conduction in metals and semiconductors, phonons and superconductivity.

PHYS 490.title: Student Directed Seminar
PHYS 490.description: Self-directed, collaborative studies, in a group-learning environment, initiated and coordinated by senior undergraduate students with the supervision of a faculty advisor. Course structure, enrolment, and delivery methods will comply with the Handbook for Student Directed Seminars. Cannot be used as a specialization requirement in any PHYS and/or ASTR specialization. .

PHYS 498.title: Co-operative Work Placement IV
PHYS 498.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the fall term of the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics.

PHYS 499.title: Co-operative Work Placement V
PHYS 499.description: Approved and supervised technical work experience in an industrial research setting for a minimum of 3.5 months. Normally taken during the summer following the fourth year. Technical report required. Restricted to students admitted to the Co-operative Education Program in Physics.

PHYS 500.title: Quantum Mechanics I
PHYS 500.description: Non-relativistic quantum mechanics with applications to atomic, nuclear and particle physics. Perturbation theory, multielectron atoms, molecular structure, WKB, scattering theory. Recommended pre-requisite: PHYS_V 402.

PHYS 501.title: Quantum Mechanics II
PHYS 501.description: Time-dependent perturbation theory, density matrix formalism, NMR, emission and absorption of radiation. Elementary field theory techniques for many body systems. Quasiparticles, phonons, magnons, holes. Relativistic Klein-Gordon and Dirac equations.

PHYS 502.title: Condensed Matter Physics I
PHYS 502.description: One-electron theory of solids, energy bands, lattice vibration, transport theory.
notes: A background in undergraduate solid state physics such as covered in PHYS_V 474 is highly recommended.

PHYS 503.title: Condensed Matter Physics II
PHYS 503.description: Interacting electrons, electron-phonon interaction, Hubbard model, magnetism, superconductivity, use of Green functions.

PHYS 504.title: Special Relativity and Classical Electromagnetism
PHYS 504.description: Boundary-value problems, Green's functions and multipole expansions, magnetostatics, Faraday's law of induction, retarded potentials, Poynting's theorem and conservation laws, gauge invariance. Propagation of electromagnetic waves. Presentation of radiation from moving charges, classical electron theory.
notes: A background in electricity and magnetism such as covered PHYS_V 401 is highly recommended.

PHYS 505.title: Nuclear Physics
PHYS 505.description: Nucleons and their structure, hadrons and isospin, two-nucleon systems and interactions, bulk properties of nuclei and models, nuclear excitations and radioactivity, strong and electromagnetic decay, symmetries and weak interaction, reactions, nuclear astrophysics.

PHYS 509.title: Theory of Measurements
PHYS 509.description: Estimation of parameters from experimental measurements; maximum likelihood; least squares; tests of significance (chi square, etc). Noise properties of common devices. Extracting signals from noise; signal averaging; auto and cross-correlation, etc.

PHYS 515.title: Modern Biophysics
PHYS 515.description: Fundamental concepts and advanced applications as used in current biophysics research.

PHYS 516.title: Statistical Mechanics
PHYS 516.description: Mean field theory, Landau theory of phase transitions, critical phenomena, renormalization theory. Monte Carlo method, linear response theory, fluctuations.

PHYS 518.title: Superconductivity
PHYS 518.description: Conventional theories: BCS and Landau-Ginsburg, Josephson effect. New theories of high TC superconductivity.

PHYS 520.title: Teaching Techniques in Physics and Astronomy
PHYS 520.description: Foundations of physics and astronomy education research, lesson plans, development of grading, effective questioning, effective presentations, methods in peer evaluation, and peer teaching. .

PHYS 521.title: Group Theory Methods in Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 521.description: Selected topics from atomic, molecular, solid state, nuclear and elementary particle physics treated by group theory methods.

PHYS 523.title: Quantum Electronics and Nonlinear Optics
PHYS 523.description: Macroscopic and microscopic treatments of linear and non-linear response to electromagnetic fields.

PHYS 525.title: Advanced Condensed Matter Physics
PHYS 525.description: Current issues in condensed matter theory.

PHYS 527.title: Topics in Nuclear Physics
PHYS 527.description: Selected topics from current nuclear theory.

PHYS 533.title: Laser Physics
PHYS 533.description: Classical and semi-classical treatment of interaction of EM-radiation with atomic systems; semi-classical laser theory; Gaussian beams and optical resonators; specific laser types and systems; femtosecond lasers and amplifiers; Raman lasers; lasing with inversion; topics of current research interest.

PHYS 534.title: Radiotherapy Physics I
PHYS 534.description: Principles of dosimetry of ionizing radiation with emphasis on applications to radiotherapy and radiobiology.

PHYS 535.title: Radiotherapy Physics II
PHYS 535.description: A continuation of PHYS_V 534, including an extension of the topics discussed in that course.

PHYS 545.title: Anatomy and Physiology for Medical Physicists
PHYS 545.description: Restricted to graduate students in the M.Sc. (Medical Physics) Specialization.

PHYS 546.title: Clinical Experience in Medical Physics
PHYS 546.description: Clinical treatment planning techniques, quality assurance of treatment equipment and clinical decision making for radiation therapy. Quality assurance and decision making for medical imaging. Pass/fail.

PHYS 555.title: Directed Studies in Physics
PHYS 555.description: With approval of the department head, advanced studies under the direction of a staff member may be arranged in special cases. Grade type may vary by section. Some sections may be Pass/Fail.

PHYS 560.title: Physics and Engineering of Particle Accelerators
PHYS 560.description: Injectors, radio frequency acceleration, superconducting acceleration elements, beam dynamics, and applications of electron accelerators.

PHYS 565.title: Applications of Radioisotopes in Science and in Medicine
PHYS 565.description: Use of radioisotopes in nuclear medicine, materials science, environmental science, and nuclear physics in combination with the associated production, processing, and detection technologies.

PHYS 573.title: Modelling and Simulation of Quantum Materials
notes: A background in undergraduate solid state physics such as covered in PHYS_V 474 is highly recommended.
